subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: Acme — GPU & throughput
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: Acme — GPU & throughput

Hi Sam / Dana,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to get a clear sense of Acme's primary latency and cost targets. Quick recap and the asks we discussed:

Summary from call:
- Workload: conversational assistants + long-context extraction for support cases (avg prompt+response ~ 1.2k tokens; peak 4k).
- Target p50 latency: <= 150ms per token (interactive), goal for p95 below 300ms.
- Throughput target: sustained 50 concurrent sessions with bursts to ~150 concurrent.
- Expected steady-state monthly consumption: ~0.9–1.5B tokens (est.), with occasional spikes tied to product launches.

Pricing / budget signals you gave
- Target unit economics goal: ~$20–$35 per 1M tokens for dedicated capacity (goal is to beat public-hosted unit cost while guaranteeing SLOs).
- Annual budget range: $300–$500k committed for inference capacity (flexible depending on SLA/term).

Open technical items we need from you to size Dedicated properly:
1) Preferred GPU family: are you leaning toward A100 (40/80GB), H100, or open to 8-bit/4-bit quantized configs on Ampere-gen? This materially affects slot throughput.
2) Desired HA / failover tolerance (single AZ vs multi-AZ) — drives how much reserved capacity we recommend.
3) Any hard SLOs for p99 (we discussed p95 but p99 targets change sizing).
4) Confirmation on retention/encryption needs that might require Private deployment (we heard you might want VPC later).

Next steps
- If you can confirm GPU preference and p99 target by EOD Thu we will run a sizing estimate and provide a 2-option pricing sheet (conservative and optimized) + a draft mutual action plan.
- Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Example.pdf (example price bands) and a blank MAP template (MAP-Acme.xlsx).

Thanks — will follow up with Marcus to include the throughput/slot mapping once you confirm GPU preference.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
--
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A few clarifications:

1) GPU preference: we are currently evaluating H100 for new workloads but given budget we are open to A100-80GB if it meets latency targets. If quantization can get us similar throughput while reducing cost we'd consider it.

2) HA: multi-AZ preferred for production; dev/staging can be single-AZ.

3) p99: ideally < 800ms, but we'll take your recommendation if it requires a higher reserve.

Budget: the $300–$500k is comfortable but we'd need to see committed throughput and clear $/1M token math before committing. Can Marcus include a mapping table showing tokens/sec per GPU type and expected $/1M tokens at each reserved tier?

Also, can you call out the burst model — how many burst slots we can expect and how long? That will affect our multi-AZ sizing.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30m if you want to walk through the numbers.

—Sam

Hi Sam — quick technical sizing table (high level). Assumptions: model = 13B-ish open family optimized for FP16/4-bit when applicable; avg end-to-end tokens per request = 1.2k; response tokens ~600 of that.
\Sizing (sustained):
- H100 (80GB)
  - effective slots/server: 1 GPU = 1 slot
  - estimated throughput: ~200 tokens/sec per slot (13B optimized), ~350 tokens/sec (8B family)
  - recommendation: for 50 sustained concurrent sessions -> target ~ (50 * 1.2k tokens) / 200 = ~300k tokens/sec aggregate -> this is incorrect, see corrected calc below.
\Corrected throughput calc:
- Per-session tokens/sec: expecting interactive at ~3 tokens/sec/user (back-and-forth), but worst-case generation at ~20 tokens/sec during heavy generation bursts.
- For 50 concurrent sessions at average 3 tokens/sec => 150 tokens/sec aggregate. At 200 tokens/sec per H100 slot, 1 slot covers the steady state comfortably; however to meet p95/p99 and headroom for loading, we recommend 3–4 H100 slots reserved (multiplied for multi-AZ + failover).
\A100-80GB (quantized workloads):
- estimated throughput: ~120 tokens/sec per slot (13B quantized), ~220 tokens/sec for 8B quantized
- recommendation: 4–6 slots reserved to meet steady-state + burst headroom; if quantization gives you 2x throughput on A100 we can optimize further.
\Cost ballpark (12mo commit) — example only, final will be in PDF:
- Conservative profile (multi-AZ, HA + 30% buffer):
  - H100: 4 reserved slots + burst policy => ~$420k/yr (~$35 per 1M tokens at 1B tokens/mo equivalent)
  - A100-80 (quantized): 6 reserved slots => ~$340k/yr (~$28 per 1M tokens)
\- Optimized profile (single-AZ prod, tighter SLOs):
  - H100: 3 slots => ~$320k/yr (~$24 per 1M tokens)
  - A100-80: 4 slots => ~$260k/yr (~$20 per 1M tokens)
\Notes & next steps:
- These numbers assume your model family and token mix; exact $/1M tokens changes with request mix, average prompt length, and real observed batching efficiency.
- If you can share a 2-week sample of production traces (anonymized token/time series) we can produce a precise cost model.
- If the budget target is $20/1M tokens, A100 quantized profiles or larger commit discounts are most likely to hit that number.
\Happy to jump on Thu AM — I'll prepare a clean table and two formal quote PDFs (conservative + optimized) after we confirm GPU and p99 target.
\Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
